archetypes.title: Tidal Cathedral Park
archetypes.description: A former drowned neighbourhood intentionally re-flooded twice daily by controlled tides. Submerged streets and piazzas emerge at low tide; stepped amphitheatres stand partially underwater; bioluminescent seagrass grows where there were once streets. An urban memorial that is also an active wetland and an inhabitable ruin — the city learning to love its own drowned form.

variants.label: Venetian Resurrection
variants.description: Mediterranean canal-city lineage. Stepped stone piazzas emerge at low tide; fragments of palazzi rise like small islands. Active fish and mollusc nurseries in the flooded streets. The city that always knew this was coming.

variants.label: Bangladesh Delta Reshore
variants.description: River delta typology. Stilted timber pavilions rise above the flooded plain; floating markets assemble at high tide. Re-established fishing villages atop the drowned older settlements. Adaptation as continuity.

variants.label: Manhattan Flood Park
variants.description: Post-flood Manhattan — subway tunnels are now coral-lined grottos; avenue amphitheatres host low-tide gatherings. The street grid preserved as a tidal pattern. Skyline still standing, feet wet.

variants.label: Pacific Atoll Coral Park
variants.description: Engineered coral colonies grown over former Pacific-island settlements. The coral is the architecture; the old paths are now reef channels. Swimmers, snorkellers, and fish share the plaza-reefs.

archetypes.title: Echo Garden
archetypes.description: A circular plaza where speech is captured, slowed, and played back across weeks via acoustic architecture — directional panels, silence wells, cross-fade zones. Your voice becomes tomorrow's context, and the garden itself is a slow-motion public discourse. A civic resource for a society that wants to listen more slowly than it speaks.

variants.label: Zen Gravel Echo
variants.description: Japanese-influenced — raked gravel around concentric timber acoustic panels; a single stone silence well at the centre. Minimalist voice-listening. Three benches for the three kinds of thought.

variants.label: Islamic Courtyard Echo
variants.description: Muqarnas-inspired acoustic niches in the rim walls; a central fountain that cross-fades the previous week's voices into water-sound. Tiled in deep blue and cream. Seating along the arcades.

variants.label: Celtic Standing Stone Echo
variants.description: Megalithic precedent — standing stones arranged as primary acoustic resonators, with engraved grooves directing sound. Moss and wildflowers in the interstices. Pre-modern technology meets post-modern acoustics.

variants.label: Modernist Parametric Plaza
variants.description: Clean concrete + parametric sound panels — the contemporary articulation. Brutalist-adjacent sculptural form, with warm inlaid timber handholds at listening stations.

archetypes.title: Pollinator Cathedral
archetypes.description: A 200-meter vertical wildflower supercluster engineered as monument-scale habitat for the last 3,000 native pollinator species. Humans access via cable-stayed catwalks between lantern-pods. Sacred and ecological in equal measure — part cathedral, part living Noah's ark for the insects that built agriculture.

variants.label: Tropical Orchid Tower
variants.description: Tropical orchid and hummingbird variant — pink, magenta, and violet orchids cover the structure. Hummingbirds and nectar-moths abound. Humid air. Golden-hour shafts of light.

variants.label: Prairie Sunflower Stack
variants.description: Great-Plains heritage — golden yellow sunflowers and goldenrods cover the tower. Monarch butterflies and native bees. Late-summer warmth.

variants.label: Alpine Wildflower Spire
variants.description: High-elevation variant — alpine wildflowers (gentians, alpine asters, edelweiss) and alpine moths. Thin clear cold air. Snow-capped peaks behind. Silver-green palette.

variants.label: Mediterranean Lavender Obelisk
variants.description: Dry-climate lavender, rosemary, and thyme variant. Silver-green and purple foliage. Honeybees and wild solitary bees. Fragrant in the heat. Olive trees at the base.

archetypes.title: Slow Park
archetypes.description: A park where time deliberately runs at 1/10 speed for visitors — via deep meditative programming, acoustic isolation, and carefully curated attention fields. No clocks, phones, or photos. Entering requires a 30-minute transition. The civic library of slowness, meant for grief, deep thought, and major life decisions. A public resource as essential as clean water.

variants.label: Japanese Moss Garden
variants.description: Moss carpets across soft undulating ground, a few thoughtful stones, a single stone basin. The slowness of moss, felt as architecture.

variants.label: European Monastic Cloister
variants.description: Walled stone herb garden, a central well, low clipped lavender, a covered arcade walk. The monastic tradition as civic resource.

variants.label: Rainforest Cathedral
variants.description: Under giant canopy trees, filtered light, tree-ferns, a single rain-pool. The pre-agricultural forest as contemplative chamber.

variants.label: Prairie Stillness
variants.description: Wide open prairie grasses under a vast sky, wind the only sound, a single bench facing the horizon. Slowness of vast space.

archetypes.title: Savanna Garden
archetypes.description: The evolutionary-optimal park — open meadow with scattered large shade trees, a watering hole, and a distant ridge on the horizon. Prospect-refuge theory perfected. Every human visual system was tuned by a million years of preferring exactly this landscape; the park is what our DNA expects to see. Reading, resting, picnicking, thinking — all deeply calibrated by this ancient ground.

variants.label: African Acacia Savanna
variants.description: Central African ancestral variant — acacia trees, tall golden grasses, gazelle herd visible, distant kopje rock-hill.

variants.label: English Oak Meadow
variants.description: Northern European variant — spreading oaks over wildflower meadow, grazing deer, stone folly.

variants.label: Prairie Cottonwood Garden
variants.description: North American prairie variant — cottonwood trees clustered near a slow creek, tallgrass prairie, bison herd in distance.

variants.label: Mediterranean Olive Savanna
variants.description: Mediterranean variant — ancient olive trees, wildflower meadow, stone outcrops, distant hilltop village.

archetypes.title: Aquarium Gardens
archetypes.description: An inhabitable aquatic-biome park you walk through via clear glass atria, with fish flocking overhead and coral or kelp framing you. Multisensory awe-machine combining water's parasympathetic calm, the blue-shift of mammalian cortisol, and the sheer sublime of an alien biosphere you can enter. Free to the public.

variants.label: Coral Reef Garden
variants.description: Tropical coral reef variant — colourful reef fish, parrotfish, sea turtles, bright coral structures.

variants.label: Kelp Forest Garden
variants.description: Pacific cold-water variant — towering giant kelp, sea lions, orange garibaldi fish, dappled green-gold light.

variants.label: Freshwater River Garden
variants.description: Temperate river variant — trout, sturgeon, pike, willows overhead above the glass, freshwater clarity.

variants.label: Arctic Ice Aquarium
variants.description: Polar variant — beluga whales, narwhals, ice caves, pale blue-white light, cold clear water.

archetypes.title: Stone Garden of Time
archetypes.description: A megalithic landscape of massive standing stones precisely aligned to celestial cycles — solstices, planetary conjunctions, specific stars' annual transits. Walking the stones is walking deep time. A civic astronomical instrument you live inside, combining the ancient resonance of standing-stone ritual with modern astronomical precision.

variants.label: Solstice Stone Circle
variants.description: Stonehenge-inspired solstice circle — trilithons aligned to summer and winter sunrises.

variants.label: Lunar Standing Stones
variants.description: Bronze-Age-inspired lunar cycle marker — tall slender stones tracking monthly phases.

variants.label: Planetary Alignment Garden
variants.description: Incan-precision stonework — finely joined polygonal stones marking planetary conjunctions.

variants.label: Southern Star Chart Garden
variants.description: Southern-hemisphere star-pattern stones — positions of stones mirror constellations overhead.

archetypes.title: Night Bloom Garden
archetypes.description: A park experienced primarily at night. Bioluminescent plants, moon-path pavements, star-observation platforms, night-blooming flowers releasing fragrance only after dusk. The sacred night that modern cities obliterated — reclaimed with modern atmospheric care (dark-sky preserves, minimal light pollution) and ancient reverence.

variants.label: Full Moon Lotus Garden
variants.description: Tropical lily-pond variant — waterlily pools, night-blooming lotus, tropical fireflies.

variants.label: New Moon Milky Way Meadow
variants.description: Dark-sky preserve — wildflower meadow under a blazing Milky Way, bioluminescent fungi in shadows.

variants.label: Blue Hour Fern Cathedral
variants.description: Temperate fern gully variant — cool blue bioluminescent mosses, tall tree ferns, small waterfalls.

variants.label: Desert Night Cactus Garden
variants.description: Arid variant — tall columnar cacti with rare night-blooming white flowers, clear desert sky.
